# Java Core & Spring Boot — Interview Notes

---

## 1. SOLID Principles

| Principle | Full Name | One-Liner |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| **S** | Single Responsibility | A class should have **only one reason to change** |
| **O** | Open-Closed | Open for **extension**, closed for **modification** |
| **L** | Liskov Substitution | Subtypes must be **substitutable** for their base types |
| **I** | Interface Segregation | Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they **don't use** |
| **D** | Dependency Inversion | Depend on **abstractions**, not on concrete implementations |

### 1.1 Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)

Every Java class must perform a **single functionality**.

```java
// GOOD — each class has one job
class UserService {
    void registerUser(User user) { /* registration logic */ }
}

class NotificationService {
    void sendEmail(String to, String msg) { /* email logic */ }
}
```

### 1.2 Open-Closed Principle (OCP)

Module should be **open for extension** but **closed for modification**.

```java
// Base class — never modify this
abstract class PaymentProcessor {
    abstract void processPayment(double amount);
}

// Extend with new processors
class CreditCardProcessor extends PaymentProcessor {
    void processPayment(double amount) { /* credit card logic */ }
}

class UPIProcessor extends PaymentProcessor {
    void processPayment(double amount) { /* UPI logic */ }
}
```

### 1.3 Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)

Derived/child classes must be **completely substitutable** for their base classes without altering the behavior.

```java
// Works because ArrayList IS-A List
List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();  // Substitution works
list.add("Hello");
```

> **Interview Tip:** If your subclass throws an exception or behaves differently from what the base class promises, you're violating LSP.

### 1.4 Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)

Larger interfaces should be **split into smaller ones**. Clients should not be forced to implement irrelevant methods.

```java
// BAD — Chef shouldn't implement serveFood() or cleanTable()
interface RestaurantWorker {
    void cookFood();
    void serveFood();
    void cleanTable();
}

// GOOD — split into focused interfaces
interface Chef { void cookFood(); }
interface Waiter { void serveFood(); }
interface Cleaner { void cleanTable(); }
```

### 1.5 Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)

High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on **abstractions**.

```java
// BAD — tight coupling to concrete class
class PaymentService {
    private CreditCardPayment payment = new CreditCardPayment(); // ❌
    void processPayment(double amount) { payment.pay(amount); }
}

// GOOD — depends on abstraction
interface Payment { void pay(double amount); }

class CreditCardPayment implements Payment {
    public void pay(double amount) { System.out.println("Paid $" + amount + " via Credit Card"); }
}

class PaymentService {
    private Payment payment; // ✅ abstraction
    PaymentService(Payment payment) { this.payment = payment; }
    void processPayment(double amount) { payment.pay(amount); }
}
```

## 2. OOP Concepts

### Core Pillars

| Pillar | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| **Inheritance** | Inheriting properties and behaviors from parent class (`extends`, `implements`) |
| **Polymorphism** | Multiple forms — same method name, different behavior |
| **Abstraction** | Hiding implementation details, exposing only essential features |
| **Encapsulation** | Wrapping data + methods in a single unit (class), hiding via access modifiers |

### Polymorphism Types

| Type | Mechanism | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| **Compile-time** | Method Overloading | Same method name, different parameters |
| **Runtime** | Method Overriding | Same method signature, different behavior in subclass |

| Method Overloading | Method Overriding |
|--------------------|-------------------|
| Multiple methods with **same name, different parameters** | Subclass provides its **own implementation** of parent's method |
| **Compile-time** polymorphism | **Runtime** polymorphism |
| In the **same class** | In **parent-child** relationship |

### Abstract Class vs Interface

| Feature | Abstract Class | Interface |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| Methods | Both abstract and non-abstract | Only abstract (default & static allowed after Java 8) |
| Instantiation | Cannot be instantiated | Cannot be instantiated |
| Inheritance | `extends` one class only | Can `implement` multiple interfaces |
| Access modifiers | Any access modifier | Methods are `public` by default |
| Variables | Can have instance variables | Only `public static final` constants |

> **When to use Abstract Class?** When sharing **common behavior** across subclasses.
> **When to use Interface?** When defining a **contract** that multiple unrelated classes can implement.

### Tricky OOP Questions

#### 1. Can a constructor be private?
**Yes** — used in **Singleton Pattern** to restrict object creation.

#### 2. Can we override a static method?
**No** — static methods belong to the **class**, not instances. **Method hiding** occurs if a subclass redefines it.

#### 3. What is `super` vs `this`?
- `super` — calls the **parent class** constructor/method
- `this` — refers to the **current instance**, calls constructor of same class

#### 4. Can an abstract class have a constructor?
**Yes** — used to **initialize common fields** before subclass constructors run.

#### 5. Can we create an object of an abstract class?
**No** — but we can create an **anonymous inner class** instance of it.

#### 6. Can we override a private method?
**No** — private methods are **not inherited**.

#### 7. `super()` vs `this()` in constructors?
- `super()` — calls **parent class** constructor
- `this()` — calls another constructor **in the same class**

## 3. The `this` Keyword

- A **reference variable** that refers to the **current object** of a class.
- Differentiates between instance variables and method parameters with the same name.

```java
class Employee {
    String name;
    Employee(String name) {
        this.name = name; // 'this.name' = instance variable, 'name' = parameter
    }
}
```

## 4. Java 17 Features

### 4.1 Sealed Classes

Allows **restricting which classes can extend** a superclass. Controls class hierarchy and improves security.

```java
sealed class Shape permits Circle, Rectangle, Triangle { }

final class Circle extends Shape { }
final class Rectangle extends Shape { }
non-sealed class Triangle extends Shape { } // can be extended further
```

![][image1]

### Sealed Class vs Final Class

| Feature | `sealed` Class (Java 17) | `final` Class |
|---------|--------------------------|---------------|
| Inheritance | **Limited** — only permitted classes can extend | **None** — no class can extend |
| Keyword | Uses `permits` to define allowed subclasses | Simply `final` |
| Use case | Control hierarchy, allow specific extensions | Ensure immutability, prevent modification |

### 4.2 Pattern Matching for Switch

```java
// Java 17 - Pattern Matching
static String describe(Object obj) {
    return switch (obj) {
        case Integer i -> "Integer: " + i;
        case String s  -> "String: " + s;
        case null      -> "null";
        default        -> "Unknown: " + obj;
    };
}
```

![][image2]

## 5. Core Java Fundamentals

### 5.1 `hashCode()` and `equals()` Contract

- `equals()` — by default compares **object reference**. Should be overridden to compare **values**.
- `hashCode()` — returns an integer that **uniquely identifies** an object (used as bucket number).

**Contract Rules:**
- If two objects are **equal** → their `hashCode()` **MUST** be the same
- If two objects are **not equal** → their `hashCode()` **CAN** be same or different

**`==` operator:**
- Compares **references** for objects (same memory location?)
- Compares **values** for primitives

```java
String s1 = new String("hello");
String s2 = new String("hello");

s1 == s2;       // false (different references)
s1.equals(s2);  // true (same content)
```

### 5.2 `final`, `finally`, `finalize`

| Keyword | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `final` | Declares constants, prevents method overriding, prevents class inheritance |
| `finally` | Block always executed after `try`, regardless of exception |
| `finalize` | Method called by GC before object is reclaimed (deprecated in Java 9+) |

### 5.3 `volatile` Keyword

- Declares variables that require **visibility across threads**.
- Changes are **immediately visible** to all threads.
- Reads and writes are **atomic** (for the variable itself, not compound operations).

```java
class SharedResource {
    volatile boolean running = true;

    void stop() { running = false; }  // visible to all threads immediately
}
```

### 5.4 `==` vs `.equals()`

| Feature | `==` | `.equals()` |
|---------|------|-------------|
| For objects | Compares **references** (memory address) | Compares **content** (logical equality) |
| For primitives | Compares **values** | Not applicable |
| Custom classes | Always reference check | Must be **overridden** for meaningful comparison |

### 5.5 `static` Keyword

- Indicates a field, method, or block belongs to the **class**, not instances.
- Shared among **all instances** of the class.
- Accessed via `ClassName.memberName`.

**Limitations:**
- Static methods **cannot** access non-static (instance) members directly
- `this` or `super` **cannot** be used in static contexts
- Static methods **cannot** be overridden (they are hidden)

```java
class Counter {
    static int count = 0; // shared across all instances
    Counter() { count++; }
    static int getCount() { return count; }
}
```

### 5.6 String vs StringBuffer vs StringBuilder

| Feature | String | StringBuffer | StringBuilder |
|---------|--------|-------------|---------------|
| Mutability | **Immutable** | **Mutable** | **Mutable** |
| Thread Safety | Thread Safe (immutable) | **Thread Safe** (synchronized) | **Not Thread Safe** |
| Performance | Creates new object on change | Slow (due to synchronization) | **Fast** |
| Use case | Few modifications | Multi-threaded string manipulation | Single-threaded string manipulation |

```java
// String — new object each time
String s = "Hello";
s = s + " World"; // new String object created

// StringBuilder — modifies same object
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Hello");
sb.append(" World"); // same object modified — faster
```

## 6. Garbage Collection & Memory Management

### 6.1 Garbage Collection (GC)

- **Automatic memory management** — identifies and removes unreferenced objects from **heap memory**.
- Before destroying an object, GC calls `finalize()` method for cleanup.
- Algorithm: **Mark and Sweep**

| GC Type | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| **Minor GC** | Collects short-lived objects from **Young Generation** |
| **Major GC** | Collects long-lived objects from **Old Generation** |
| **Full GC** | Collects from **all generations** — causes app pause |

### 6.2 Java Memory Model

![][image3]

Memory is split into: **Heap** and **Metaspace** (formerly PermGen, since Java 8).

#### Metaspace
- Stores **class metadata** (method names, fields, modifiers)
- Stores **static variables**
- Stores **Constant Pool** (runtime constants, method references)
- JVM flags: `MetaspaceSize` (initial), `MaxMetaspaceSize` (max allowed)

```java
class Example {
    static int x = 10;    // Stored in Metaspace
    String name;           // Stored in Heap (inside object)

    void display() {
        int local = 5;     // Stored in Stack
    }
}
```

![][image4]
![][image5]

#### Heap
- Stores **objects** (created with `new` keyword)
- Stores **data structures** — Arrays, Collections (`new ArrayList<>()`)
- Divided into **Young Generation** and **Old Generation**

![][image6]

**Young Generation:**
- Divided into **Eden Space** + **2 Survivor Spaces** (S0, S1)
- Objects initially allocated in **Eden**
- When Eden is full → **Minor GC** → survivors move to S0/S1
- Objects surviving multiple GC cycles → **promoted to Old Generation**

**Old Generation (Tenured):**
- Stores **long-lived objects** that survived multiple Minor GCs
- **Major GC** performed here to reclaim memory

**JVM Heap Flags:**
- `-Xms` → initial heap size
- `-Xmx` → maximum heap size

### 6.3 JVM Memory Storage Summary

| Area | Stores |
|------|--------|
| **Heap** | Objects created at runtime (via `new`) |
| **Stack** | Local variables, method call stack, partial results |
| **Metaspace** | Class metadata, static variables, constant pool |
| **Native Method Stack** | Native methods used in the application |

### 6.4 Memory Leaks

**Definition:** Objects no longer needed remain referenced, preventing GC from collecting them.

**Common Causes:**

```java
// 1. Static collections never released
static List<String> cache = new ArrayList<>(); // grows forever

// 2. Unclosed streams/connections
FileInputStream fis = new FileInputStream("file.txt");
// If not closed → memory leak!
fis.close(); // always close in finally or use try-with-resources

// 3. Overuse of caches (Maps not cleared)
Map<Integer, String> cache = new HashMap<>();
cache.put(1, "data"); // keys never removed = memory grows

// 4. Unclosed DB connections
```

**Prevention & Monitoring:**
- Use **try-with-resources** for streams/connections
- Use **WeakHashMap** for caches
- Monitor with: **Prometheus, Grafana, New Relic**
- Configure **logging and alerting** for memory thresholds (Log4j, SLF4J)

## 7. Serialization

- **Serialization** — converting an object into a **byte stream** (to save in file/DB or send over network)
- **Deserialization** — converting byte stream **back into an object**
- Class must implement `Serializable` interface

![][image7]

### `serialVersionUID`
- Unique identifier ensuring **version compatibility** during deserialization
- If mismatch → `InvalidClassException`

### `transient` Keyword
- Prevents a field from being serialized

```java
class User implements Serializable {
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
    String username;
    transient String password; // NOT serialized — null after deserialization
}
```

## 8. Java 8 Features

### Overview

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Functional Interface** | Interface with single abstract method |
| **Lambda Expression** | Anonymous function — instance of functional interface |
| **Stream API** | Pipeline processing of collections |
| **Optional** | Wrapper to handle null values safely |
| **Method Reference** | Compact way to refer to a method (`::`) |
| **Default Method** | Methods with implementation inside interfaces |
| **Java DateTime API** | New `java.time` package |

### 8.1 Lambda Expression

An **anonymous function** that can be assigned to a variable or passed as an argument.

```java
// Syntax: (parameters) -> expression

// Before Java 8
Comparator<String> comp = new Comparator<String>() {
    public int compare(String a, String b) { return a.compareTo(b); }
};

// With Lambda
Comparator<String> comp = (a, b) -> a.compareTo(b);
```

![][image8]

- Represents instances of **Functional Interfaces**
- Can be passed as parameters to methods
- Does not belong to any class — standalone
- Receives type when assigned to a functional interface

### 8.2 Method Reference

Compact way to refer to a method using `::` (double colon).

```java
// Lambda
Function<String, Integer> parser = (str) -> Integer.parseInt(str);

// Method Reference (equivalent)
Function<String, Integer> parser = Integer::parseInt;

// Types of method references:
// ClassName::staticMethod     → Integer::parseInt
// object::instanceMethod      → str::toUpperCase
// ClassName::instanceMethod   → String::toUpperCase
// ClassName::new              → ArrayList::new
```

### 8.3 Optional<T>

Represents a value that **may or may not be present**. Avoids `NullPointerException`.

```java
Optional<String> name = Optional.of("John");       // non-null value
Optional<String> empty = Optional.empty();         // no value
Optional<String> nullable = Optional.ofNullable(null); // may be null

// Methods
name.isPresent();           // true
name.get();                 // "John"
empty.orElse("Default");   // "Default"
nullable.orElseThrow();    // throws NoSuchElementException
```

### 8.4 Functional Interface

Interface with **only one abstract method**. Can have multiple default/static methods.

| Interface | Input | Output | Use |
|-----------|-------|--------|-----|
| `Consumer<T>` | T | void | Perform action, no return |
| `Supplier<T>` | None | T | Produce a value |
| `Predicate<T>` | T | boolean | Test a condition |
| `Function<T,R>` | T | R | Transform input to output |

```java
// Consumer — takes input, no output
Consumer<String> print = name -> System.out.println(name.toUpperCase());
print.accept("john"); // JOHN

// Supplier — no input, returns output
Supplier<Integer> random = () -> new Random().nextInt(100);
random.get(); // random number 0-99

// Predicate — takes input, returns boolean
Predicate<Integer> isEven = num -> num % 2 == 0;
isEven.test(10); // true

// Function — takes input, returns transformed output
Function<String, Integer> length = str -> str.length();
length.apply("Hello"); // 5
```

### 8.5 Streams API

A **sequence of elements** processed in a functional pipeline using lambda expressions.

**Key Methods:** `filter()`, `map()`, `flatMap()`, `reduce()`, `sorted()`, `collect()`, `forEach()`

```java
List<String> names = Arrays.asList("John", "Alice", "Bob", "Charlie");

// Filter + Map + Collect
List<String> result = names.stream()
    .filter(name -> name.length() > 3)        // keep names with length > 3
    .map(String::toUpperCase)                   // transform to uppercase
    .sorted()                                   // sort alphabetically
    .collect(Collectors.toList());              // collect to list
// Result: [ALICE, CHARLIE, JOHN]
```

### 8.6 Map vs Filter vs Reduce

| Operation | Purpose | Input | Output |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `map()` | **Transform** each element | Stream\<T\> | Stream\<R\> |
| `filter()` | **Select** elements matching condition | Stream\<T\> | Stream\<T\> |
| `reduce()` | **Aggregate** to single value | Stream\<T\> | T (single value) |

```java
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);

// filter — keep even numbers
numbers.stream().filter(n -> n % 2 == 0).toList(); // [2, 4, 6]

// map — square each number
numbers.stream().map(n -> n * n).toList(); // [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36]

// reduce — sum all
numbers.stream().reduce(0, Integer::sum); // 21
```

### 8.7 map() vs flatMap()

| Feature | `map()` | `flatMap()` |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| Mapping | One-to-one | One-to-many |
| Flattening | Does NOT flatten nested structures | **Flattens** result into single stream |
| Use case | Transform each element | Flatten nested lists/streams |

```java
List<String> words = List.of("Hello", "World");

// map — gives Stream<Stream<Character>> (nested!)
// flatMap — gives Stream<Character> (flattened!)
List<Character> chars = words.stream()
    .flatMap(word -> word.chars().mapToObj(c -> (char) c))
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
// [H, e, l, l, o, W, o, r, l, d]
```

### 8.8 Comparator vs Comparable

| Feature | Comparable | Comparator |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Purpose | **Natural ordering** | **Custom sorting** |
| Method | `compareTo()` | `compare()` |
| Implementation | Class itself implements it | External class/lambda |
| Compares | Current object with another of **same class** | Two objects of **same or different** classes |
| Package | `java.lang` | `java.util` |

```java
// Comparable — natural ordering (inside the class)
class Employee implements Comparable<Employee> {
    String name; int age;
    public int compareTo(Employee other) { return this.name.compareTo(other.name); }
}

// Comparator — custom sorting (external)
employees.sort(Comparator.comparing(Employee::getName).reversed());
```

![][image9]
![][image10]

### 8.9 Converting Arrays/Lists to Streams

```java
// Array to Stream
String[] arr = {"test1", "test2", "abc"};
String[] filtered = Arrays.stream(arr)
    .filter(s -> s.startsWith("test"))
    .toArray(String[]::new);

// List to Stream
List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
List<String> result = list.stream()
    .filter(e -> e.equals("prasad"))
    .toList();

// Array ↔ List conversions
String[] arr2 = list.toArray(new String[0]);   // List → Array
List<String> list2 = Arrays.asList(arr);       // Array → List

// Sort by name descending
employees.sort(Comparator.comparing(Employee::getName).reversed());
```

## 9. Exception Handling

### throw vs throws

| Feature | `throw` | `throws` |
|---------|---------|----------|
| Purpose | **Explicitly throw** an exception | **Declare** that a method might throw exceptions |
| Location | Inside method body | Method **signature** |
| Usage | Both checked and unchecked exceptions | Only **checked** exceptions |
| Example | `throw new ArithmeticException("Error");` | `public void read() throws IOException { }` |

### Custom Exceptions

```java
// Checked Exception — must be handled by caller
public class UserNotFoundException extends Exception {
    public UserNotFoundException(String message) {
        super(message);
    }
}

// Usage
public User findUser(int id) throws UserNotFoundException {
    User user = userRepository.findById(id);
    if (user == null) throw new UserNotFoundException("User not found: " + id);
    return user;
}
```

### Centralized Exception Handling (Spring Boot)

Uses `@ControllerAdvice` + `@ExceptionHandler` — manage exceptions in **one place**.

![][image11]
![][image12]

```java
@RestControllerAdvice
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {

    @ExceptionHandler(UserNotFoundException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleUserNotFound(UserNotFoundException ex) {
        ErrorResponse error = new ErrorResponse("NOT_FOUND", ex.getMessage());
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND).body(error);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleGeneral(Exception ex) {
        ErrorResponse error = new ErrorResponse("INTERNAL_ERROR", "Something went wrong");
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR).body(error);
    }
}
```

## 10. Spring Boot Basics

### @Component vs @Service vs @Bean

| Annotation | What it does |
|------------|-------------|
| `@Component` | Marks a class as a Spring-managed bean (auto-detected via component scanning) |
| `@Service` | Specialization of `@Component` — indicates **business logic** layer |
| `@Repository` | Specialization of `@Component` — indicates **data access** layer |
| `@Bean` | Denotes a **method** that explicitly defines a bean in a `@Configuration` class |

![][image13]

```java
@Service
public class UserService { /* business logic */ }

@Configuration
public class AppConfig {
    @Bean
    public RestTemplate restTemplate() { return new RestTemplate(); }
}
```

### Profiles in Spring Boot

Profiles allow **environment-specific configuration** (dev, test, prod).

```java
@Bean
@Profile("dev")
public DataSource devDataSource() { return new H2DataSource(); }

@Bean
@Profile("prod")
public DataSource prodDataSource() { return new PostgresDataSource(); }
```

**Checking Active Profile in Code:**
```java
@Component
public class ProfileCheck {
    @Value("${DB_URL:default_value}")
    private String dbUrl;

    private final Environment env;

    public ProfileCheck(Environment env) {
        this.env = env;
        String[] activeProfiles = env.getActiveProfiles();
        String dbUrl = env.getProperty("DB_URL");
    }
}
```

**Set active profile:** `spring.profiles.active=dev` in `application.properties`

## 11. Collections

### 11.1 HashMap

- Stores data in **(key, value)** pairs. Uses **Array + LinkedList** internally.
- **Not Synchronized** (faster than Hashtable)
- **Duplicate keys not allowed** — replaces existing value
- Average **O(1)** time for get/put operations
- Capacity: **16**, Load factor: **0.75**
- Allows **one null key** and multiple null values

![][image14]

#### Internal Working

Each node contains:

| Hash | Key | Value | Next |
|------|-----|-------|------|

- **Buckets** = array of nodes (LinkedList at each bucket)
- `put("Prasad", 26)` → calculate `hashCode("Prasad")` → compute index: `hashCode & (n-1)`
- Store entry at that bucket index

#### Hash Collision

When 2+ keys have the **same index**:
1. Check if keys are **equal** using `equals()` → replace value
2. If keys are **different** → add to **LinkedList** at that bucket (or **TreeNode** after 8 entries in Java 8+)

#### get() Method
1. Calculate `hashCode` of key → get index
2. Traverse LinkedList at that bucket → compare keys using `equals()`
3. Return matching value

### 11.2 HashMap vs TreeMap vs HashTable

| Feature | HashMap | TreeMap | HashTable |
|---------|---------|---------|-----------|
| Implementation | **Hash table** | **Red-Black Tree** | **Hash table** |
| Performance | O(1) average | **O(log n)** | O(1) average |
| Ordering | **No order** | **Sorted** (natural or comparator) | **No order** |
| Null keys | One null key | **No null key** | **No null key** |
| Thread safety | **Not synchronized** | **Not synchronized** | **Synchronized** |
| Use case | Fast lookup/insert | Sorted iteration needed | Legacy thread-safe map |

![][image15]

### 11.3 ArrayList

- Implemented as a **resizable/dynamic array**
- **Not synchronized**, high performance
- **Initial capacity: 10**
- Preserves **insertion order**
- When full: creates new bigger array → copies all elements → uses new array reference

### 11.4 ArrayList vs LinkedList

| Feature | ArrayList | LinkedList |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Implementation | **Dynamic array** (contiguous memory) | **Doubly linked list** (non-contiguous) |
| Random access (get) | **Fast** — O(1) | **Slow** — O(n) |
| Insert/Delete (start/mid) | **Slow** — shifting required | **Fast** — pointer manipulation |
| Memory | More efficient | Less efficient (extra pointers) |
| Best for | **Storing and accessing** | **Frequent insertion/deletion** |
| Interface | List only | **List + Queue (Deque)** |

### 11.5 Set

Collections that **don't store duplicate elements** and generally don't maintain order.

| Type | Implementation | Ordering | Performance |
|------|---------------|----------|-------------|
| **HashSet** | Hash table (HashMap internally) | **No order** | O(1) |
| **LinkedHashSet** | Hash table + Doubly linked list | **Insertion order** | O(1) |
| **TreeSet** | Red-Black tree | **Sorted order** | O(log n) |

### 11.6 HashSet Internals

- Internally uses **HashMap** — element stored as **key**, value is constant `"PRESENT"`
- Uses hash function to map element to bucket index

| Key (Element) | Value |
|---------------|-------|
| "John" | PRESENT |
| "Alice" | PRESENT |

## 12. JVM Architecture

### ClassLoader
- Part of **JRE** — loads Java classes (`.class` files) into JVM at runtime

### JVM
- Part of **JRE** — converts **bytecode** (platform independent) into **machine code** (platform dependent)

### JRE
- Provides **runtime environment** (RAM, libraries) to execute Java programs

### JDK
- Complete package: **JRE** + **Development Tools** (compiler `javac`, debugger, etc.)

```
JDK ⊃ JRE ⊃ JVM
```

## 13. Maven

Build automation tool for Java projects. Manages dependencies, build lifecycle, and plugins.

![][image16]
![][image17]

**Key Concepts:**
- `pom.xml` — Project Object Model (configuration file)
- **Dependencies** — libraries needed (downloaded from Maven Central)
- **Build Lifecycle** — `compile` → `test` → `package` → `install` → `deploy`
- **Plugins** — extend Maven functionality

## 14. Monolithic vs Microservices

| Feature | Monolithic | Microservices |
|---------|-----------|---------------|
| Structure | **Single codebase** | **Small independent services** |
| Scalability | Limited (scale entire app) | **Highly scalable** (scale individual services) |
| Deployment | Deploy as **whole** | Deploy **independently** |
| Fault tolerance | Failure affects **whole** app | **Isolated failures** |
| Tech stack | Single technology | **Polyglot** (different tech per service) |
| Communication | In-process method calls | REST/gRPC/Message queues |

---

## 15. Singleton Design Pattern (Creational)

Ensures **only one instance** of a class exists throughout the application and provides a **global access point**.

```java
public class DatabaseConnection {
    private static volatile DatabaseConnection instance;

    private DatabaseConnection() { } // private constructor — no external instantiation

    public static DatabaseConnection getInstance() {
        if (instance == null) {                       // first check (no lock)
            synchronized (DatabaseConnection.class) {
                if (instance == null) {               // second check (with lock)
                    instance = new DatabaseConnection();
                }
            }
        }
        return instance;
    }
}
```

> **Use case:** DB connection pool, Logger, Configuration manager

---

## 16. Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy

| Feature | Shallow Copy | Deep Copy |
|---------|-------------|-----------|
| Object fields | Copies **references** (same objects) | Creates **new copies** of referenced objects |
| Nested objects | Shared between original and copy | **Independent** — changes don't affect each other |
| Performance | Faster | Slower (more memory) |

```java
// Shallow — address object is shared
Employee copy = original.clone(); // copy.address == original.address

// Deep — new address object created
Employee deepCopy = new Employee(original.name, new Address(original.address));
```

## 17. Real-Life Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Frequency Count Program

**Problem:** Count character/word frequency using Java 8 Streams.

```java
String input = "hello world hello java";
Map<String, Long> freq = Arrays.stream(input.split(" "))
    .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), Collectors.counting()));
// {hello=2, world=1, java=1}
```

### Scenario 2: Sort Employees by Name (Descending)

```java
List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
    new Employee("John", 25),
    new Employee("Alice", 30),
    new Employee("Bob", 22)
);
employees.sort(Comparator.comparing(Employee::getName).reversed());
// [John, Bob, Alice]
```

### Scenario 3: Memory Leak Detection in Production

- **Symptom:** Application slows down over time, eventually `OutOfMemoryError`
- **Diagnosis:** Use Prometheus/Grafana dashboards, check heap usage trends
- **Common causes:** Static collections, unclosed connections, listener leaks
- **Fix:** Profile with VisualVM/JProfiler, identify retained objects, fix references

### Scenario 4: Choosing HashMap vs TreeMap

- Need **fast lookup** without ordering → **HashMap** (O(1))
- Need **sorted iteration** (e.g., range queries, leaderboard) → **TreeMap** (O(log n))
- Need **thread safety** → `ConcurrentHashMap` (not Hashtable!)

### Scenario 5: Handling NullPointerException Across Codebase

- Use `Optional<>` for methods that might return null
- Use `@NonNull` / `@Nullable` annotations
- Centralized null checks at API layer (validate inputs early)
- Use `Objects.requireNonNull()` for fail-fast

## 18. Top 15 Frequently Asked Interview Questions (4 Years Exp — Product-Based)

### SOLID & OOP

**Q1. Explain SOLID principles with examples. Which principle is most violated in your experience?**

> Cover all 5 with code examples. Most commonly violated: **SRP** (god classes) and **DIP** (tight coupling to concrete classes).

**Follow-up:** How would you refactor a class violating SRP?

---

**Q2. What is the difference between Abstract Class and Interface? When would you use each?**

> Abstract class = shared behavior + state; Interface = contract, multiple inheritance. Since Java 8, interfaces can have default methods — blurring the line.

**Follow-up:** Can an abstract class implement an interface? (Yes!)

---

**Q3. Explain Runtime vs Compile-time polymorphism with real code.**

> Compile-time = overloading (same name, different params). Runtime = overriding (subclass redefines parent method, resolved at runtime via virtual method table).

**Follow-up:** What is method hiding in static methods?

---

### Core Java & Memory

**Q4. What is the `hashCode()` and `equals()` contract? What happens if you override one but not the other?**

> If `equals()` is overridden without `hashCode()`, equal objects may end up in different HashMap buckets → get() won't find them.

**Follow-up:** What happens to a HashMap if two keys have the same hashCode?

---

**Q5. Explain Java Memory Model — Heap, Stack, Metaspace. Where are objects/primitives stored?**

> Objects → Heap. Local primitives/references → Stack. Class metadata, static → Metaspace. String pool → Heap (since Java 7).

**Follow-up:** What is a memory leak? How do you detect one in production?

---

**Q6. What's the difference between `==` and `.equals()`? Why does `new String("abc") == new String("abc")` return false?**

> `==` checks reference equality. `.equals()` checks content. Two `new String` objects are different references in heap.

**Follow-up:** What about String pool? `"abc" == "abc"` returns true — why?

---

### Java 8 & Streams

**Q7. What are Functional Interfaces? Name the built-in ones and when you'd use each.**

> Single abstract method. Consumer (void action), Supplier (produce value), Predicate (boolean test), Function (transform).

**Follow-up:** Can a functional interface have multiple default methods? (Yes!)

---

**Q8. Explain `map()` vs `flatMap()` in Streams with an example.**

> `map()` = 1:1 transform. `flatMap()` = 1:many + flatten. Use flatMap when stream operations return nested collections/streams.

**Follow-up:** What is a lazy vs eager operation in Streams?

---

**Q9. How would you find the second-highest salary from a list of employees using Streams?**

```java
Optional<Integer> secondHighest = employees.stream()
    .map(Employee::getSalary)
    .distinct()
    .sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder())
    .skip(1)
    .findFirst();
```

**Follow-up:** What if there are duplicates? What if list has < 2 elements?

---

### Collections & Data Structures

**Q10. Explain internal working of HashMap. What happens during a put() call?**

> hashCode() → index calculation → check bucket → equals() for collision → store/replace. After Java 8: LinkedList → TreeNode (>8 entries).

**Follow-up:** What is the default load factor? What happens during rehashing?

---

**Q11. ArrayList vs LinkedList — when would you choose one over the other?**

> ArrayList = fast random access (O(1) get). LinkedList = fast insert/delete at head/middle (O(1) remove). ArrayList is almost always better in practice (cache locality).

**Follow-up:** What happens internally when ArrayList capacity is exceeded?

---

**Q12. What is the difference between Comparable and Comparator? When to use which?**

> Comparable = natural order (inside class, one sorting logic). Comparator = custom/multiple orderings (external, flexible).

**Follow-up:** How do you sort by multiple fields? (Comparator.comparing().thenComparing())

---

### Exception Handling & Spring

**Q13. How do you handle exceptions globally in Spring Boot? What's the difference between @ControllerAdvice and @ExceptionHandler?**

> `@ControllerAdvice` = global handler class. `@ExceptionHandler` = handles specific exception type. Together they provide centralized, clean error handling.

**Follow-up:** How would you return different error formats for REST vs web views?

---

**Q14. Explain `throw` vs `throws`. What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?**

> `throw` = explicitly throw. `throws` = declare in signature. Checked = must handle (IOException). Unchecked = runtime (NullPointerException).

**Follow-up:** Should you catch RuntimeException? When?

---

### Design & Architecture

**Q15. Explain Singleton pattern. What's the problem with naive implementation in multi-threaded environment?**

> Naive: two threads can create two instances. Fix: double-checked locking + volatile. Or use enum singleton (thread-safe, serialization-safe).

**Follow-up:** How does Spring Boot manage singletons differently? (IoC container manages bean lifecycle)
